what: New layout rule: app content capped at 1440px by the shared layout
why: Future pages must not re-introduce per-page width caps that drift from the app-wide standard
summary: Recorded the 1440px content-cap convention as a rule (shared `.app-main > :global(*)` lever in +layout.svelte + `--max-width: 90rem`; never per-page max-width, /pages 1024px cap removed). Updated the design-system entity page with the Layout token line and a 2026-09-15 lifecycle entry.

user: Data-dense pages can now go full width with a single class instead of custom width CSS
what: Documented the full-bleed class as the only sanctioned way to exempt a page from the shared 1440px cap
why: Keeps all page widths controlled by one lever and one opt-out, preventing per-page max-width drift
summary: Extended the 1440px layout rule to document the new full-bleed opt-out class (.app-main > :global(.full-bleed) { max-width: none }) added in PR #4; listed the four full-bleed routes (/analyst, /data, /page/<slug>, /pages).

user: Data Analyst and Data pages now use your full screen width
what: /analyst and /data are exempt from the 1440px content cap and span the whole window, matching the page editor
why: Wide tables and chat surfaces benefit from every pixel of horizontal space
next: Open /analyst or /data on a wide screen

user: The Pages overview is now full width with a responsive card grid
what: /pages was rebuilt: full width, cards reflow from 1 up to 4 columns by screen size, each card shows title, slug, updated date, and a delete-on-hover with confirmation
why: More pages visible at once and page management (scan, delete) is faster on wide screens
next: Open /pages and resize the window to see columns adapt

user: Creating a page now opens a proper modal with a live URL preview
what: The + New page button opens a modal: title field with live slug preview (/page/your-slug), Enter creates the page, Escape / backdrop / X closes it — replacing the always-visible inline title input
why: A cleaner Pages overview and clearer intent when starting a new page; the URL is visible before you commit

user: All buttons and links now show the hand pointer cursor across the whole app
what: Added one global CSS rule so every interactive element (buttons, links, selects, tabs) shows the pointer cursor; verified across /pages, /data, /analyst, /settings, and /labs/bar-chart with zero exceptions.
why: On Windows, buttons showed an arrow cursor by default, making them feel non-clickable.
next: Hover any button or link — the pointer cursor now appears everywhere.

user: Page cards on /pages are more compact — glanceable in 3 rows
what: Page cards on /pages were compacted to at most 3 rows: the icon now floats top-right, the date sits inline with the page slug, and an empty footer row was added for breathing room.
why: The cards were too tall and airy; the new layout fits more pages on screen at a glance.
next: Open /pages to see the denser card grid.

user: Developers now have one documented place for cursor styling: a single global rule in app.css
what: Added wiki rule: pointer cursor comes from one global rule in app.css.
why: Prevents per-component cursor styles from drifting as new interactive elements are added.
summary: Recorded the app-wide pointer-cursor convention as a rule: one global selector list in src/app.css covers all interactive affordances; no per-component cursor styles. Disabled controls excluded.

what: Documented the page-editor route move (/page/<slug> → /pages/<slug>) and the /data full-width change; updated the stale 1440-cap rule.
why: Q16 and the layout rule documented the old route and old centering mechanism — future sessions and e2e tests would target the wrong URL or mis-diagnose full-bleed shrinkage.
summary: Recorded the /pages/<slug> route restructure (supersedes Q16's /page/<slug>), the flex-column auto-margin shrink-to-fit gotcha behind the full-bleed fix, and patched the 1440-cap rule to reflect the new width:100% mechanism and route path.

user: The AI agent will never start or restart the dev app on its own — it asks you and waits
what: Added a wiki preference: LLM must not launch npm run dev / tauri dev; if it needs the app running (CDP checks, e2e, visual QA) it must say so and wait for the user
why: LLM-driven kill/restart cycles caused stale-HMR webviews that looked like real bugs and disrupted the user's window
summary: Recorded user-stated preference: the LLM must never start npm run dev / npx tauri dev / background dev servers — it asks the user ("Please start the app") and waits instead. Motivated by stale-HMR webviews and recycled CDP debug ports from LLM-driven restart churn.
